channel.title: WritOn — Stories, Thinking & Independent Essays
channel.description: Curated independent essays, craft reflections, poetry, and ideas on modern culture. Read 700+ literary stories on WritOn.

item.title: Escaping the Walled Garden: When Open-Source Software Depends on Proprietary Gates
item.dc:creator: Riya Sharma
item.description: The tension facing community-funded software like AnkiDroid demonstrates that open-source code cannot guarantee autonomy if distribution remains trapped behind proprietary app store tollbooths.

item.title: Canopy and Solitude: Why Gardens Are Becoming Literary Commons
item.dc:creator: Radhika Gowda
item.description: Silent-reading gatherings in public gardens across Indian cities reveal an appetite for uncomplicated presence: a non-transactional third space where people can be together without continuously performing sociability.

item.dc:creator: Ananya Bose

item.dc:creator: Karthik Subramanian
item.description: AI dramatically reduces the cost of producing code, but writing software has never been the entire cost of software. When throwaway scripts quietly harden into unmaintained infrastructure, understanding becomes the hidden debt.

item.title: The Witnessed Sentence: Why the Short Story Matters in the Age of Synthetic Prose
item.dc:creator: Arshdeep Singh (Arsh Zee)
item.description: When synthetic detail becomes computationally cheap, specificity is no longer proof of humanity. The short story endures because it preserves accountable selection: an actual author who had an urgent human reason to arrange the room that way.

item.dc:creator: Dr. Sunita Banerjee

item.title: The Review Debt of the Automated Pull Request
item.dc:creator: Devansh Roy
item.description: When the marginal cost of producing code falls to zero while verification remains human and expensive, open-source maintainers face an asymmetric denial of attention. Contribution without accountability is simply review debt created in someone else’s name.

item.title: The Cognitive Fast: The Case for Coding Without an Assistant
item.dc:creator: Aarav Mehta
item.description: When AI assistance generates code faster than an engineer can mentally simulate its operational edge cases, debugging intuition degrades. There is a case for the deliberate, periodic fast from coding assistants to protect the internal models that production systems demand.
